newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stock index futures end with sharp losses.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stock index futures end with sharp losses.

text.p: U.S. stock index futures closed sharply lower and near the daily lows as worries about higher interest rates steadily pushed the market down during the course of the session.

"There were rate worries," said Jay Hohmann, head futures trader at Donaldson, Lufkin and Jenrette Securities, who also noted that "the technicals were set up to have the market move lower. Chart patterns had a downard bias."
Hohmann said that not only the cash S&P 500 index but individual stocks such as Intel broke below key support levels.
Intel shares broke a key level at $135.00, while the cash S&P 500 index fell below 740.00. "The 720 level in cash (S&P 500s) is the next level to be looking at," Hohmann said.
"We have a well-defined down-channel and we're at the bottom of it now," Hohmann said. "At current levels and at its position in the channel, the next move in the market is "a tough call," he said.
Concern about higher interest rates gathered momentum early in the day after the March core U.S. producer price index rose by 0.4 percent compared to expectations for a rise of about 0.1 percent.

The higher than expected inflation figure prompted selling in the bond market, which in turned pushed the June S&P contract down the 7.00-point opening limit in the first 10 minutes of the pit session.
Selling continued at a steady pace during the morning, and June S&P 500s reached their second daily limit of down 15.00 points by midday.
Premiums narrowed on the decline, at times triggering arbitrage sell programs that fueled declines in cash stocks, traders said.
Still, traders said two large brokerage houses were noted buyers during the day, and the decline overall was very orderly.
Nikkei 225 stock index futures posted sizable gains early, then slipped in tandem with U.S. stocks, but staged a relatively strong comeback at the close to end higher.

At settlement, June S&P 500s were off 24.85 points at 738.50, Nasdaq 100s were 26.90 lower at 797.00, Russell 2000s were down 8.05 points at 340.10, KCBT Value Line futures were down 14.95 points at 677.70, Nikkei 225 index futures rose 200.0 to 17,690.0 and Midcap 400s fell 6.75 points to 249.30.
